# @AUTOGENERATED by scripts/gen_scarcity.py — do not edit; run script to regenerate.
# Defines SOL_compute_scarcity_score_<strata> (location scope) for 5 strata,
# plus the market-hub orchestrator SOL_update_market_scarcity_scores.
#
# Per-stratum budget-share-weighted correction.
# Delta formula: -(1 - 1/P_tier) × alpha_avg[strata][group] / n_goods_in_group
# where alpha_avg = mean budget share across all 4 income brackets.
#
# Natural bounds (all goods in a single tier simultaneously):
#   shortage max: -(1 - 1/2.30) = -0.5652  →  adj = 0.435 (never negative)
#   surplus  max: +(1/0.40 - 1) = +1.5000  →  adj = 2.500
# No hard cap applied; demand scales have min = 0 as safety floor.
#
# Caching strategy: the score depends ONLY on the location's market (all 336
# checks are market ?= { ... }), so identical work would repeat for every
# location sharing a market. Instead we run the score effects ONCE per market,
# at the market's hub location (market.location), and downstream readers in
# SOL_pop_values.txt fetch via market.location.var:sol_market_scarcity_adj_*.

# Market-hub orchestrator — call from root scope on the global yearly tick.
# Iterates ~600 markets (vs 4000+ owned locations), so this is the
# load-bearing optimization for January performance.
SOL_update_market_scarcity_scores = {
	every_market_in_world = {
		location = {
			limit = { is_land = yes }
			SOL_compute_scarcity_score_nobles = yes
			SOL_compute_scarcity_score_clergy = yes
			SOL_compute_scarcity_score_burghers = yes
			SOL_compute_scarcity_score_commoners = yes
			SOL_compute_scarcity_score_tribesmen = yes
		}
	}
}
